title: Compass and Regiment
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, 1799, Sable Sterling, a mapmaker's apprentice of uncertain birth, is completing the master cartographer's forbidden atlas—maps of smuggling routes, garrison weaknesses, and the Governor's secret land claims—when an infant is left at the workshop door with a note: forget the face. The child is the illegitimate heir of the Governor, and the atlas is the proof of everything he has stolen. As the century turns, Sable must choose between burning the atlas to save the workshop and finishing it to give the child an inheritance of truth, ending with Sable publishing the atlas under their own name and raising the child as the workshop's true legacy.
about_author: Quentin Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial-era maps before turning to fiction. They write about the people history forgot to name, and live within sight of a harbor that no longer appears on modern charts.

chapters.title: The Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ten years after Master Corvane's suspicious death, Sable works alone finishing the atlas in secret, memorizing which rooms creak and which neighbors report. Establishes the workshop as home and the atlas as both inheritance and danger. Emotional beat: quiet devotion laced with fear.

chapters.title: A Bundle at the Door
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. On the winter solstice, an infant is left at the workshop with a note reading 'forget the face' and a scrap of embroidered silk. Sable, who knows every rule of silence, breaks the first one by keeping the child. Emotional beat: tenderness arriving like an intrusion.

chapters.title: The Governor's Surveyor
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with a brief letter from Governor Aldous Vane. A royal surveyor arrives requesting Corvane's papers, polite as a blade. Sable lies for the first time in ten years. Emotional beat: the realization that the atlas was never finished—it was hidden.

chapters.title: What the Silk Says
chapters.summary: Sable's POV with neighbor Maren's perspective interwoven. The embroidered silk matches a crest Sable once inked onto a suppressed map: Vane's own. The child is his. Maren, a laundress who sees everything, agrees to help. Emotional beat: complicity becoming alliance.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silences
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Sable's POV. How Sable came to the workshop as a debt-orphan, how Corvane taught that a map is a confession, and the night he died after refusing to surrender the coastal charts. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Atlas's Missing Leaf
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable discovers one folio of the atlas is missing—the map of the Governor's forged land grants. Corvane hid it, and someone else is looking. A break-in leaves the workshop searched but untouched. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing they are hunted.

chapters.title: Milk and Gunpowder
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Daily life with the baby inside a conspiracy: feeding her, hiding her cries during inspections. Maren's own lost child surfaces in memory. Emotional beat: motherhood as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Surveyor's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Surveyor Hale returns, revealing he knows the atlas exists and offers Sable a bargain: the missing leaf for safe passage out of Vellamare. Sable reads Hale's hands, not his words, and sees a man as trapped as they are. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a honest face.

chapters.title: Charts of the Drowned Quarter
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following Corvane's marginalia, Sable searches the flooded old harbor district where the master once surveyed for Vane, finding a hidden cache—and evidence Vane drowned a village to erase its land claims. Emotional beat: horror at what beauty was made to conceal.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. New Year's Eve, 1800: fireworks, bells, and the whole city watching the sky while Sable watches the door. The baby's first birthday. Vane's men mark the workshop. Emotional beat: celebration shadowed by countdown.

chapters.title: Hale's Confession
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The surveyor reveals he was ordered to find and destroy the atlas, and that Corvane's death was no accident—he was the one who reported the master, believing it would save him. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution it cannot have.

chapters.title: The Price of the Leaf
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable negotiates with Hale: passage and silence in exchange for a copy of the missing leaf, keeping the original. But copying it means inking the proof that could hang them both. Emotional beat: the weight of every stroke.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Vane's steward offers Maren money to reveal where the child sleeps. She takes the coin and gives a lie, then realizes the workshop will be raided within days. Emotional beat: courage disguised as a transaction.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Soldiers seize the workshop and burn the visible atlases. Sable, forewarned, has moved the true atlas into the one place no one looks: bound inside a finished, worthless atlas of Vane's own commissioned parks. Emotional beat: loss and triumph in the same breath.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Vane himself questions Sable, and the scene becomes a duel of silences—each knowing what the other knows, neither able to prove it. Vane offers legitimacy: a post, a name, a place to belong. Emotional beat: the corruption of belonging offered as a gift.

chapters.title: What Sable Sterling Wants
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Released but watched, Sable confronts the truth: they have always wanted a name, a lineage, a place—and Vane offered exactly that. The chapter turns on the decision to refuse an inheritance bought with a drowned village. Emotional beat: identity chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Printers of Salt Lane
chapters.summary: Sable and Maren's POV. They find a radical printer willing to engrave the atlas's key plates, trading secrecy for the truth about the drowned quarter. Hale, defecting, brings the original survey notes as corroboration. Emotional beat: fragile, conspiratorial hope.

chapters.title: The Governor's Error
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The Governor learns the atlas survives, and his response is not caution but fury—he orders the workshop district burned, corrupting even his loyalists. His own surveyor is marked for death. Emotional beat: power devouring itself.

chapters.title: Fire on Salt Lane
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The press is burned; the printer dies shielding the plates. Hale takes a bullet meant for Sable, dying with the atlas's truth in his coat. Maren escapes with the baby; Sable with the original. Emotional beat: grief as fuel.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Atlas
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the cathedral crypt, before magistrates Vane cannot buy, Sable unbinds the atlas and reads it aloud: the forged grants, the drowned quarter, the child's name inked in the margin in Corvane's hand—proof the master knew and protected her. Emotional beat: the climax, silence finally broken.

chapters.title: The Fall of a Cartographer's Governor
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Vane's grants are voided; he flees rather than face trial, his name struck from the very maps he corrupted. The workshop is restored to Sable by charter. Emotional beat: justice arriving quietly, like weather.

chapters.title: The Atlas Under a New Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, years later. The atlas is published bearing two names: Corvane's and Sable Sterling's. The child, Elowen, learns to draw coastlines at the workbench. Sable inks a new chart of Vellamare that includes, for the first time, the drowned quarter. Emotional beat: belonging built, not inherited.
